claims.text: In a disordered bcc high-entropy alloy, Tc is predominantly controlled by electron-phonon coupling.
Heavy-element isotopic substitution will predictably shift Tc in accordance with BCS theory.
Ti-Zr-Hf-Nb-Mo can serve as a single-phase, disordered bcc HEA with every element at or above 5 atomic percent.
Natural-Zr and heavier-isotope-enriched samples can be compared while holding elemental composition and processing conditions constant.
XRD and electron microscopy can be used to verify phase purity and comparable microstructure between the isotope-control samples.
The relevant structural mediator is the phonon spectrum, particularly vibrational modes associated with the isotopically substituted element.
Within BCS theory, Tc depends in part on electron-phonon coupling and the phonon-frequency spectrum.
Increasing isotopic mass lowers the corresponding phonon frequencies.
The isotope-induced decrease in phonon frequencies reduces electron-phonon coupling strength.
Reduced electron-phonon coupling from heavier isotopes will lower Tc.
The isotopically enriched HEA will exhibit a measurable, likely negative shift in Tc relative to the natural-isotope baseline.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to samples that remain disordered, bcc, single-phase, and nominally electronically unchanged by isotope substitution.
The magnitude of the Tc shift is uncertain because of possible subtle microstructural variation and non-uniform electron-phonon coupling among constituents.
Failure to observe a significant systematic lowering of Tc, or observation of an increase in Tc, after phase and microstructure are controlled would falsify the proposed isotope-mediated mechanism.
